open_points.subject: Manifest document consumed by bindings operations
open_points.text: A ManifestOperation M10 is read from the one entry of the record's `capabilities` whose `name` equals the operation name, together with the `api_base_url` and `required_headers` of the instance the installation selects for that service
open_points.question: What exact JSON structure, field types and optionality does a service manifest use for capabilities, instances, exposed HTTP routes, required headers, instance classes and idempotency keys?
options: Capabilities and instances are arrays, and required headers are an ordered list of name/value pairs
Capabilities and instances are objects keyed by name, and required headers are an object
The kernel consumes an external manifest schema that must be named explicitly
open_points.default_guess: Use an explicit schema with capability and instance arrays and required headers as a list so duplicate names remain detectable.

open_points.subject: Manifest revision reading
open_points.text: the platform manifest is read at — read by every manifest reading (M10), so a record changes for the kernel only when the owner changes the configured revision
open_points.question: How must bindings read `<manifest_location>/<service_id>.json` at `manifest_revision`, rather than silently reading some other filesystem state?
options: Read the file directly from the named Git object or tree at that revision
Require `manifest_location` to be an already materialized immutable snapshot and verify its revision
Read the current working-tree file and treat the revision as informational
open_points.default_guess: Read the file from the repository object identified by `manifest_revision`, without consulting working-tree contents.

open_points.subject: bindings.check_installed_instances
open_points.text: an unreadable record, or one failing a check of the record itself (A08 rule 5), fails at its service
open_points.question: Which A08 rule 5 checks apply at startup when this operation has a service and selected instance but no operation name or proposed ports?
options: Only service-level structure, duplicate capability names and the selected instance's header facts
Every capability in the record must pass all operation-record checks that do not require proposal ports
Select an operation by an unstated rule and apply its checks
open_points.default_guess: Check service-level structure, duplicate capability names and selected-instance facts; leave operation-specific checks to proposal, acceptance and send.

open_points.subject: Service api_base_url
open_points.text: The URL is the `api_base_url` without a trailing `/` followed by the declared path
open_points.question: Are user information, query, fragment and non-root base paths allowed in `api_base_url`, and exactly how are trailing slashes and the operation path combined?
options: Restrict the base URL to scheme, authority and an optional path with no query, fragment or user information, then concatenate deterministically
Allow all absolute URLs and use RFC URL resolution
Allow all absolute URLs and concatenate their text after stripping trailing slashes
open_points.default_guess: Reject user information, query and fragment; preserve an optional base path and remove all trailing slashes before appending the declared path.

open_points.subject: Declared HTTP path
open_points.text: Placeholder values are percent-encoded so that they stay one segment. Nothing else is normalized.
open_points.question: What characters and percent escapes are valid in the literal portions of a declared path, and are those literals sent verbatim, percent-encoded, or refused when they are not already a valid URI path?
options: Require literal path text to be valid ASCII URI-path syntax with valid percent escapes and send it verbatim
UTF-8 percent-encode every literal path segment
Pass the manifest text directly to the HTTP library and accept its normalization
open_points.default_guess: Require valid URI-path syntax, preserve valid literal text and escapes, and percent-encode only substituted placeholder values.

open_points.subject: Multipart input port names
open_points.text: `Content-Disposition: form-data; name="<port>"`, with `filename="<port>"` added for a file part
open_points.question: How are quotes, backslashes, control characters and non-ASCII characters in a port name represented or refused in multipart `name` and `filename` parameters?
options: Restrict multipart port names to a closed safe character set
Apply a specified quoted-string escaping and encoding rule
Insert the port text verbatim
open_points.default_guess: Reject CR, LF and controls and use a specified quoted-string escaping rule for quotes and backslashes.

open_points.subject: Header and credential text validation
open_points.text: whose value is empty, has leading or trailing whitespace, or holds a control character
open_points.question: Which exact Unicode or byte characters count as whitespace and control characters for required-header and credential validation?
options: HTTP ASCII rules: leading or trailing SP/HTAB and ASCII control bytes including DEL
All Unicode whitespace and Unicode control categories
The HTTP library's own header-value validation
open_points.default_guess: Use explicit HTTP ASCII rules: SP/HTAB for surrounding whitespace and ASCII controls 0x00–0x1F plus 0x7F.

open_points.subject: Credential trailing newline removal
open_points.text: its content decoded as UTF-8, without one trailing newline, is the value
open_points.question: Does one trailing newline mean LF only, one CRLF sequence, either LF or CRLF, and are additional trailing newline sequences retained or removed?
options: Remove exactly one terminal LF and a preceding CR when present
Remove exactly one terminal LF only
Strip every terminal CR and LF
open_points.default_guess: Remove exactly one terminal newline sequence, treating CRLF as one sequence and otherwise removing one LF.

open_points.subject: Plain HTTP loopback exception
open_points.text: or one whose `api_base_url` host is a loopback address
open_points.question: Is loopback determined only from a literal IP address in the URL, from special hostnames such as `localhost`, or after DNS resolution?
options: Only literal IPv4 or IPv6 loopback addresses
Literal loopback addresses and `localhost`
Every address returned by DNS must be loopback
open_points.default_guess: Allow only literal IPv4 or IPv6 loopback addresses.

open_points.subject: NodeExecution diagnostic code
open_points.text: Details of an element that concluded `operation_failed` ... are a closed set too ... Other details: `value_too_large`, `cleanup_failed`, `applied_outputs_unknown` ... M23 has `failure_detail`: bounded, without secrets, when not succeeded
open_points.question: Where is the machine-significant detail code stored or returned separately from the bounded service or exception text in `failure_detail`?
options: Add a separate `detail_code` field to NodeExecution and derived conclusions
Put the closed code into `failure_detail`, replacing any diagnostic body or exception text
Return the code only from the immediate operation and do not preserve it in the trace
open_points.default_guess: Keep a separate optional `detail_code`; retain `failure_detail` for bounded diagnostic text, while `applied_outputs_unknown` remains a derived conclusion code.

open_points.subject: Direct record-read operation outputs
open_points.text: `bindings.read_binding`: Return one binding ... Outputs: Its status, service, operation, effect class, key fields, ports with classes, pinned digest. `functions.read_contract_version`: Return one contract version as it is recorded ... Outputs: Its ports and bounds. `flows.read_flow_version`: Return one flow version's graph.
open_points.question: Do these reads return the complete State 1 record, including identity, owner links, creator or author and timestamps, or only the fields individually listed in each Outputs section?
options: Return the complete State 1 record
Return only each operation's listed projection
Return a full record to surface and a smaller projection to internal callers
open_points.default_guess: Return the complete record and let callers ignore or mask fields they do not expose.

open_points.subject: Masked failure_detail length
open_points.text: a classified `failure_detail` its length and class
open_points.question: Is the disclosed length the number of UTF-8 bytes, Unicode scalar values, or characters after replacement and truncation?
options: UTF-8 byte length of the stored bounded detail
Unicode scalar-value count
Client-visible character or grapheme count
open_points.default_guess: Return the UTF-8 byte length of the stored bounded detail.

open_points.subject: SpooledFile identity and lookup
open_points.text: M22 says `Identity: value` and `equal facts are the same spooled file`, where its facts include content digest, size, media type and disclosure class; State 5 says `read_spooled_file` names it by its identity — `run_id`, `producer_node_id`, `map_index`, `attempt_number`, `producer_port`, `list_index`
open_points.question: Is a SpooledFile's public identity all M22 meaning facts or only the producing-position key listed by `read_spooled_file`?
options: The producing-position tuple is the identity and the other facts are attributes
All M22 facts form the identity, although the positional subset is a unique lookup key
Introduce a separate derived SpooledFile identifier
open_points.default_guess: Treat the producing-position tuple as the stable public identity and the digest, size, media type and class as attributes.

open_points.subject: Store privacy checks
open_points.text: private directory; no symbolic link anywhere
open_points.question: What exact ownership, permission and traversal checks make the data directory and everything in it private, including subdirectories, regular files, ACLs and unexpected file types?
options: Require kernel-user ownership and no group or other permission bits on every traversed entry
Check only the root directory's ownership and mode, relying on no-follow opens below it
Use effective-access checks including ACLs for every entry
open_points.default_guess: Require kernel-user ownership, reject group or other permissions, reject unexpected special files, and open every path component without following links.
